comments.text:
I absolutely love that you tried traditional Norwegian dishes—the kind Norwegians make at home. Eating this type of food in restaurants is expensive, so we usually cook it ourselves. When foreigners visit Norway, they tend to opt for international dishes because they are cheaper, or they buy lackluster cafeteria food that lacks flavor—and that often becomes the impression they are left with regarding Norwegian cuisine. The dishes you chose are authentically Norwegian. 
I recommend visiting Rorbua restaurant at Aker Brygge to try *boknafisk*, a dish made from semi-dried *Skrei* (spawning cod from Lofoten). They also serve *bacalao*; although originally a Portuguese dish, it is made using Norwegian *klippfisk*—salted and dried cod from Southern Norway. Consequently, the dish has become deeply rooted in Norway as well, given that we supply the raw ingredients.
